general_background.title: Making a soluble cadmium feed
general_background.summary: A carboxylic acid such as oleic acid can convert cadmium oxide into cadmium carboxylate in the flask. Changing this soluble feed and the free acid changes cadmium availability during nucleation and growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Formation of High-Quality CdTe, CdSe, and CdS Nanocrystals Using CdO as Precursor

general_background.title: Lead chloride and sulfur supply distinct growth species in oleylamine
general_background.summary: When colloidal lead sulfide is grown from a lead halide and sulfur in oleylamine, the amine environment affects sulfur activation and coordination of the soluble metal feed. Their relative availability can affect particle growth and the nature of the resulting surface.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Monodisperse, Air-Stable PbS Nanocrystals via Precursor Stoichiometry Control

general_background.title: Oleylamine changes how sulfur is delivered
general_background.summary: An amine can convert elemental sulfur into soluble polysulfide species before metal sulfide nanocrystals form. How sulfur is made available from that solution affects whether new nuclei form or existing particles keep growing.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: From Sulfur−Amine Solutions to Metal Sulfide Nanocrystals: Peering into the Oleylamine−Sulfur Black Box

general_background.title: A phosphine can carry a chalcogen feed
general_background.summary: Trioctylphosphine can solubilize elemental selenium or tellurium as a phosphine chalcogenide for colloidal growth. Delivering the chalcogen in this bonded form changes the chemistry that supplies reactive growth species.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
